title: Minimal-impact notice and replay choices — partner-ready draft
content:
Purpose:
This draft is intended for customers and partners impacted by the 2026-05-19 intermittent inference queue delay that affected a subset of tenant requests for ~45 minutes. The goal is to provide a concise status-page style update plus clear, low-friction replay and verification options customers can take to reconcile any missed or delayed inference workstreams.

Audience and tone:
- Audience: technical product owners, engineering contacts at affected customers, partner success managers.
- Tone: concise, operational, action-oriented. Minimize engineering jargon; make steps explicit.

TL;DR (one-paragraph summary):
On 2026-05-19 at ~14:03 UTC we observed a transient queuing backlog in the inference router that caused elevated request latency and a minority of requests to be delayed beyond tenant SLOs for approximately 45 minutes. The issue was caused by a rare interaction between autoscaling cooldowns and a KV-cache eviction storm; mitigation and partial fixes were deployed by 14:50 UTC and full service normalcy was verified by 15:10 UTC. If you saw failed or delayed responses during that window, you have three straightforward options (auto-replay via our self-serve tool, manual replay using our evidence package, or accept no-action) — instructions below. We will also credit impacted API usage where appropriate (see Compensation section).

What happened (plain-language timeline):
- 14:02 UTC — small spike in long sequences and a cache churn event (unexpected pattern from a subset of large-context workloads).
- 14:03–14:20 UTC — router autoscale cooldown delayed pod spin-up; queue depth increased on a small percentage (~2–3%) of requests, observed token-generation slowdowns and a few timeouts.
- 14:20–14:35 UTC — SRE mitigations: temporary routing-to-secondary-pool for high-latency tenants and manual increase of replica counts for affected pools. Partial recovery observed.
- 14:35–14:50 UTC — kernel-level cache policy adjustments rolled; queue drained for most tenants.
- 14:50–15:10 UTC — monitoring verification and gradual rollback of emergency routing. Post-deployment checks show normal latency distribution. Incident ticket INF-4729 opened and linked.

Who was affected:
- Impact was limited to specific tenants with heavy long-context, write-heavy traffic patterns that triggered rapid KV-cache invalidation.
- We estimate ~1.9% of total API requests during the window saw delays beyond their configured SLO (p50/p95 remained within normal ranges for most tenants).
- If you integrate via server-side retries or idempotent request patterns, you may have seen implicit recovery with no visible action needed.

Customer-visible effects (examples):
- Delayed streaming tokens or longer-than-usual TTF (time-to-first-token).
- Some requests returned 504s or connection resets if client timeouts were tight.
- Structured responses were preserved where possible; there were no partial truncations that we observed en masse.

Immediate actions you can take (recommended order):
1) Self-serve auto-replay (recommended for most customers):
   - Navigate to: https://console.redwood.ai/tenant-replay (requires org-admin role).
   - Select incident INF-4729 and the time window 2026-05-19 14:02–15:12 UTC.
   - The tool will present a list of requests we captured, with an "auto-replay" checkbox. Selecting auto-replay will replay requests back to your model routing with throttled concurrency to avoid causing downstream hotspots.
   - Expected time to complete: depends on request count; small customers typically finish in <10 minutes.

2) Manual replay with evidence bundle (for partners requiring auditability):
   - Download evidence package from linked artifacts (Confluence: INF-4729 investigation page). Package includes request IDs, timestamps, input payloads, and hash-sums.
   - Replay using our CLI: redwood replay --evidence <pkg> --concurrency 4 --until-complete. We recommend a conservative concurrency for large tenants.

3) No action / accept as-is:
   - If your app uses best-effort responses or you already employ retries, you may choose to take no action. If you'd like a list of affected request IDs for your internal review, request one via support and we will provide a filtered CSV.

Verification checklist (what to look for after replay):
- Request counts align with expected volumes for the window.
- p50/p95 latency returns to baseline for replayed requests.
- Response payloads match prior expectations; structured output should validate against your schema.

Safety and data integrity notes:
- We do not modify customer payloads when replaying; the evidence package contains exact request payloads and hashes.
- Replays are idempotent where possible; however, customers with non-idempotent downstream side effects should replay into a staging or sandbox route or use our "sandbox-rewrite" option to redact or tag requests.

Compensation and billing adjustments:
- We will issue a partial credit for observed failed requests (504s/timeouts) tied to the incident window. Credits will be applied to the next billing cycle and reflected as line items named "INF-4729 customer credit".
- If you require a faster, bespoke billing reconciliation, escalate to your account manager or contact partner-support@redwood.ai with "INF-4729 billing" in the subject.

How we fixed it (summary for technical contacts):
- Root cause: interaction between autoscaler cooldown thresholds and a rapid KV cache eviction pattern from long-sequence workloads caused delayed pod provisioning and elevated queueing on the router.
- Short-term fix: raised autoscale concurrency thresholds for affected pools, applied conservative KV-cache retention adjustments to reduce eviction storms, and shifted impacted tenants to secondary routing while capacity increased.
- Medium-term plan: autoscaler tuning (INF-4801) and a QoS-based router admission control to prioritize small/latency-sensitive requests during capacity churn. We will publish planned changes on Confluence and the status page.

Support & escalation paths:
- Self-serve console: https://console.redwood.ai/tenant-replay
- Support email: support@redwood.ai (subject: INF-4729)
- Partner success: partners@redwood.ai
- For high-priority enterprise escalations, reply to your designated account manager and mark "URGENT: INF-4729 impact".

Suggested status-page update copy (short):
- Title: Brief service degradation for a subset of inference requests — resolved
- Body: Between 14:03–15:10 UTC on 2026-05-19, a routing queue backlog caused delayed request processing for a small subset of tenants. The issue has been mitigated and normal service verified. We provide a self-serve replay tool and evidence packages; see https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-05-19-14 for full details and customer actions.

Suggested customer email subject lines (pick one):
- "Action recommended: Replay option available for 2026-05-19 inference delays"
- "Resolved: short service delay — replay & verification options"

Open questions / follow-ups for internal owners (SRE & Product):
- Confirm planned rollout timeline for QoS admission control (INF-4801).
- Validate compensation thresholds and aggregation across enterprise billing accounts.
- Add a short script in the replay tool that auto-detects non-idempotent request signatures and warns customers prior to replay.

Draft sign-off checklist before sending to customers:
- [ ] Legal review for wording of compensation notice (Finance copied).
- [ ] SRE verification of final monitoring snapshot (attach graphs).
- [ ] Product approval for suggested customer UX language on replay tool.
- [ ] Confirm support routing and SLA for requests created in the next 72 hours.

Notes for internal reviewers: please focus feedback on the replay UX instructions and the billing language. If you want to shorten the notice further for mass emails, propose a 2-sentence summary plus a link to the console and status page.

Document history:
- Drafted by Ethan Cole 2026-05-19
- Reviewed by Priya Nambiar and Liam Zhang 2026-05-21
- Updated with verification checklist and billing language 2026-05-22

End of draft.
